subject: Dedicated capacity planning — prompt/response audit & baseline playbook
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@heliolabs.com>, ops@heliolabs.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity planning — prompt/response audit & baseline playbook

Hi Maya / Helio ops team,

Great to connect on the Helio Labs Dedicated inquiry. To produce a tight capacity and cost baseline we'll need a short audit of your traffic and prompt/response characteristics. If you can return the items below (or point us to a sheet), we can turn this into a 1-week provisioning playbook and a low-risk canary plan: 

Requested items (ideally for a 30-day sample window):
- Average and peak concurrent sessions (p50/p95) by hour of day
- Request mix by endpoint (chat/generation/embeddings/rerank) as percentages
- Prompt length distribution (tokens): p50/p75/p95 and a couple representative examples
- Response length distribution (tokens): same percentiles + sample responses
- Typical session duration and whether KV-caching or session affinity is used
- Burst profile: longest sustained burst (minutes) and approximate request/sec during burst
- SLAs/latency targets (p50/p95 per token or per response) and cost target per generated 1k tokens
- Any hard constraints (VPC-only, KMS/HSM, data residency)

We're attaching a short CSV template you can drop numbers into (sample_traffic.csv). For context: if your p95 concurrent sessions are <200 and prompt+response tokens are typically <512, a single A10x2 style pool with autoscale + prefix cache usually covers steady state plus 3x burst headroom. If you expect long sessions with large KV caches we may recommend pinned A100s or larger memory SKUs.

Next steps:
1) Fill the small template and return by EOD Tue so we can run a 1-2 day sizing pass.
2) We’ll produce a baseline_estimate.xlsx with GPU SKU suggestions + cost curves.

Happy to jump on a 30-min technical deep-dive if helpful.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: sample_traffic.csv (CSV template), helio_requirements.pdf (requested checklist)

From: Maya Singh <maya@heliolabs.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — prompt/response audit & baseline playbook

Thanks Kimberly — attaching a filled copy of sample_traffic.csv and a short notes file. Quick answers up-front to accelerate the sizing: 

- Average concurrent sessions: 65 across US daytime; p95 concurrent sessions: 420 during marketing promotions
- Endpoint mix: chat/generation 70%, embeddings 20%, rerank 10%
- Prompt tokens: p50 48, p75 120, p95 610 (we have a long-tail of analysis prompts)
- Response tokens: p50 120, p75 420, p95 1400 (summaries + multi-paragraph outputs)
- Session duration: median 2.3 minutes; however some enterprise sessions persist for ~30 minutes (interactive analytics)
- KV caching: we do per-session retrieval caching; affinity: yes (sticky sessions per user for 10min)
- Burst profile: sustained 12-minute bursts at ~250 rps during promotions; rare spikes to ~800 rps for <2 minutes
- Latency targets: p95 end-to-end <= 1.5s for chat/generation; embeddings p95 <= 2s; cost target is < $0.15 per 1k generated tokens (aspirational)
- Constraints: VPC-first, SOC2 attestation required, customer-managed KMS preferred

Notes: We currently run a custom open model (fork of an LLM) with mixed precision -- not a managed OpenAI endpoint. We're flexible on SKU recommendations as long as memory + NVLink options are available for KV cache.

I'll schedule time for a technical call next week but wanted the template back ASAP. Attached: filled_sample_traffic.csv.

Best,
Maya
Director of ML Ops, Helio Labs
maya@heliolabs.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 06 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — prompt/response audit & baseline playbook

Thanks Maya — the numbers are very helpful. A few follow-ups and an initial hypothesis we can validate quickly: 

Quick clarifying questions:
- For the p95 1400 token responses: are those generated in a single pass or do you stream multiple inference calls per response?
- For the 30-minute interactive sessions, does the KV cache grow unbounded per session, or do you evict after N items? If unbounded we need to budget memory headroom per session.

Initial sizing hypothesis (very conservative):
- Steady state (p95 ~420 concurrent, avg tokens ~200 roundtrip): ~8 x 80GB GPUs (A10/A100 ratio depends on model memory footprint) with 2:1 oversubscription to hit cost targets.
- Burst headroom for 800 rps spikes: add transient burst pool (GPUs with fast attach) or pre-warm 4 additional GPUs for the ~2-minute spikes to avoid cold start throttling.
- For long responses (>=1k tokens): throughput per GPU drops; we should consider sequence-slicing + streaming to meet p95 latency.

I attached a quick baseline_estimate.xlsx with two scenarios: "memory-heavy" (favor A100 80GB) and "throughput-heavy" (A10-style cards with more instances). The sheet includes rough p95 latency and cost curves for each scenario.

Operational notes to include in the playbook:
- Session affinity TTLs and KV eviction policies; recommend a 10-minute TTL with LRU capped at 500 cached keys per session as an initial guardrail.
- Autoscale policy: CPU-based warmup + request queue depth triggers + pre-warm threshold at 80% utilization.
- Fallback policy: when Dedicated pool saturated, walk traffic to a compatible smaller hosted model to preserve availability (we can map equivalents).

Happy to run a small benchmark if you can provide a representative model artifact or a container image.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer

Appreciate the quick data. A few commercial considerations to help you plan: 
- We can quote both Reserved Dedicated pools (monthly commit) and a Managed Dedicated (flex with burst credits). For your burst profile the flex option can be cheaper for the first 12 months.
- Pricing note: A100 80GB baseline SKU estimate in my spreadsheet assumes $X/hr (I’ll attach a guestimate in the Doc we produce).
- SLA: we can offer a 99.9% uptime SLA on Dedicated with an Incident Response addendum for VPC customers.

Action items I’ll own this week:
1) Produce a combined baseline_estimate.xlsx with pricing curves for reserved vs flex and recommended SKU mix (A100-heavy vs A10-mix).
2) Populate a one-page rollout plan (canary scope, telemetry hooks, rollback criteria).
3) Share a DocuSign for an NDA + SOW starter if you want to lock in a pilot window.

I’ll put a draft in HubSpot and share the DocuSign link by EOD Mon. If the team wants tighter cost numbers we should run a 2-hour on-prem benchmark or let Karthik run a synthetic load with the model container.

—Marissa

Thanks all — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Quick answers to follow-ups: 
- The 1k+ token responses are single-pass generation, not stitched from multiple calls.
- KV cache: we cap per-session cache at 2,000 keys and TTL of 20 minutes; eviction is LRU. We can reduce to 500 if you recommend.

We’re comfortable moving to a pilot. Next steps from our side:
- NDA + pilot SOW review (please send DocuSign)
- Schedule a 90-minute on-site bake-off in SF the week of Jun 21 to validate latency and model fidelity on your suggested SKU mix

I’ll sign the NDA on receipt and coordinate internal stakeholders for the on-site. Thanks for the fast turnaround.

Best,
